title: Backstop Autoscale Policy Architecture for Dedicated Fleets (throughput guarantees & safety)
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
Design a conservative, production-safe autoscaling policy layer ("ops backstop") for Dedicated fleets that enforces throughput guarantees while preventing runaway scaling. The backstop sits on top of existing autoscalers and provides multi-tenant safety controls, deterministic surge caps, and a metric-composition targeter used to translate tenant throughput contracts into scale intents.

Goals:
- Ensure committed throughput contracts (tokens/sec or requests/sec) are met with bounded latency regressions.
- Prevent uncontrolled capacity growth from noisy signals or traffic spikes.
- Provide predictable, auditable scale actions with fast rollback and minimal churn.
- Enable per-tenant economic limits (max surge, monthly surge budget) and operator overrides.

Non-goals:
- Replace per-fleet primary autoscaler (PI/quantile controller). Backstop only enforces hard limits and safety policies.

Target metrics and signal composition:
- Primary throughput target: sustained tokens_per_sec over a sliding 60s window (tenant-scoped).
- Latency guard: p95 decode latency for tenant's model variant (30s window) must not exceed SLA*1.15 when scaling.
- Queue depth: request queue length above configured headroom triggers scale intent but is rate-limited.
- Error ratio: 5xx rate > 1% for 2 consecutive windows suppresses aggressive scale (indicates degradation).
- Headroom credit ledger: tracks pre-authorized token-rate headroom (seconds of prewarmed capacity) per tenant. Credits decay and are replenished on stable healthy traffic.

Scaling algorithm (hybrid approach):
- Short-term: a damped proportional-integral (PI) controller that converts composite metric gap (contract - observed throughput + queue pressure) into a desired instance delta. Controller includes slew-rate limits.
- Mid-term: quantile-based smoothing that looks at 95th percentile of recent controller outputs over 5 minutes to avoid reacting to outliers.
- Predictive warmup: when historical weekly pattern matches current ramp, pre-assign a small warm lane to reduce cold-start latency (policy uses lightweight demand forecast).
- Fallback: when primary model variant is overloaded or unavailable, automatically route to backfill variants where tenant policy permits; backstop enforces throughput fraction preserved.

Safety limits and enforcement:
- Absolute cap: per-tenant max_instances cap set by purchase tier and operator configuration.
- Surge factor: a burst multiplier defaulting to 1.25 (configurable up to 1.5 for enterpriseworks) that bounds instantaneous scale above committed baseline.
- Cooldown windows: minimum 90s between successive upscales and 600s between downscales for the backstop to avoid oscillation.
- Rollback sentinel: if p95 latency or error rate crosses predefined thresholds post-scale, trigger an automated rollback within 2x delay budget and mark a mitigation ticket.
- Auditability: every backstop decision emits a typed event (intent, evaluated signals, adjudication reason, pre/post capacity snapshot) to the Console events stream for debugging and billing reconciliation.

Operator controls & overrides:
- Emergency hold: operators can freeze scaling for a tenant or region via Console with an audit log.
- Soft-budget: monthly surge budget editable per tenant; alerting when 75% consumed.
- Simulation mode: a dry-run that emits recommended scale actions without applying them; used for rollout and SRE rehearsals.

Acceptance criteria (release candidate):
1) Backstop enforces per-tenant max_instances and surge_factor in a staging fleet with synthetic workloads.
2) Under controlled spike tests, committed throughput remains >= 95% of contract while p95 latency does not exceed SLA*1.15 more than 3% of samples.
3) Automated rollback triggers on post-scale error-rate increase and is logged as an event that links to a generated mitigation ticket.
4) Console surface for per-tenant headroom credits, surge budget, and last 30 days of backstop events exists and matches event stream.
5) Simulation mode produces identical recommended intents for 95% of replayed historical windows vs. production decisions.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for policy math and credit ledger.
- Replay tests against 30-day traffic traces from three tenants (low, bursty mid-market, enterprise steady-high).
- Chaos injection: artificially increase decode latency to validate rollback behavior.
- Staging e2e: enable backstop for a subset of dedicated fleets and run load tests with gradual 10x spikes.

Operational notes:
- Telemetry: new metrics (backstop.intent_count, backstop.rollback_count, backstop.headroom_consumed) are required; tag by tenant and region.
- Cost: headroom warm lanes should be chargeable under dedicated billing; coordinate with finance to map credits to dollar consumption.
- Migration: default backstop policy is opt-in for early customers; plan opt-out path and communication doc for customers.

Open questions:
- How to reconcile headroom credits with tenant autoscale budgets billed monthly? (work with finance).
- Tuning defaults: what is conservative surge_factor for mid-market? (suggest 1.15).
- Should predictive warmup be enabled by default for models with >60s cold-start?
comments: 2026-02-09 - Asha Patel: Initial draft posted. Major design choices called out: PI short-term controller + quantile smoothing + headroom ledger. Looking for feedback on signal weighting.
2026-02-11 - Marco Rivera: Reviewed. Suggest reducing downscale cooldown from 600s to 300s for fleets with very bursty traffic — but keep rollback sentinel strict. Added a TODO for sim results.
2026-02-13 - Priya Sharma (SRE): SRE concerns: audit events must include pre-scale capacity hash to validate billing; also want a separate metric for suppressed_scales due to error-rate gating.

2026-02-15 - Design review (Zoe Kim): UX: Console should show a time-series of headroom credit consumption and the projected next-day budget burn; captured in design doc https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Backstop+Console+UX (draft).

2026-02-18 - Marco Rivera: Spike work started. Implementing controller sim harness and replay against tenant traces. Branch: github.com/redwood-inference/backstop/tree/feature/ENG-665432 (PR forthcoming: #1287).
2026-02-20 - Asha Patel: Added acceptance criteria and test plan. Marking security_review_required = true because scaling decisions interact with billing and capacity isolation.
2026-02-20 - Security (Lina Chen): Acknowledged. We'll schedule a short threat modeling session to ensure audit/event integrity and RBAC on operator overrides.
